comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 Dutch Chemistry OER, ordinary route; prospective year pages are separately indicative 2027–2028
comparator.sourceNotes: External allocation rechecked 2026-10-08 against the adopted Dutch 2026–2027 OER, Articles 7.3–7.5 (pp.16–19). The Dutch regulation prevails over its translation and catalogue. The ordinary route totals 60 EC first-year requirements + 66 EC later requirements + 36 EC conditioned choice + 12 EC Bachelor Internship and Report + 6 EC genuinely free bachelor-level choice = 180 EC. Academic Writing in the Molecular Sciences is one 3-EC requirement. Writing about Science is not an additional universal requirement; Article 8.1 supplies replacement rules, and Article 7.4 separately permits nonoverlapping optional content. The 36-EC choice normally comprises Science-faculty bachelor courses with at least 12 EC from list BC1, or an approved minor subject to the remaining-space Chemistry minimum; it is not unrestricted open space. The previously selected RNA Structure and Function and Magnetic Resonance I (6 EC each) are retained as permitted BC1 instances. The remaining 24 EC is instantiated by the first six other distinct BC1 entries in formal list order: Advanced Molecular Biology 6, Applied Quantum Chemistry 3, Biophysical Chemistry 3, Catalysis 3, Chemical Biology Lab 3 and Chemometrics 6. This all-BC1 example satisfies the minimum without assuming a minor or optimizing against UCR. Minor exclusions in Article 7.7 remain applicable to other choices. List BC1 warns that not all options run every year; an actual timetable and enrolment must meet the catalogue requirements, and no availability guarantee is asserted. Year placement follows the indicative pages where consistent; formal Articles 7.4–7.5 govern the later-year aggregate, not a guaranteed entrant timetable. First-year Academic Skills at 0 EC is embedded in the later 3-EC Academic Skills requirement and is not added twice. PPO is embedded within credited courses. No formal named specialization is claimed. The original UCR assessment and checkedOn date remain unchanged; only its external credit description is corrected.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The molecular, cellular and biomedical programme is the strongest complete related-fields response to molecular, medicinal, laboratory and data interests. Sustainable materials and environmental applications support a distinct second route through biochemistry, geochemistry, circularity, resources and quantitative science. The next direction, synthetic and physical chemistry, fails because UCR lacks organic and inorganic chemistry sequences, synthesis, thermodynamics, quantum chemistry, spectroscopy and specialist chemistry laboratories. Production stops at two.

notes.text: Radboud Chemistry requires cumulative analytical, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics, synthesis and analysis laboratories, specialist chemistry options and a chemistry research internship. UCR can combine molecular and biomedical life science with quantitative methods, or pursue biochemistry, environmental materials and sustainable systems. These are related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the Chemistry curriculum.

The external programme has a fixed chemistry and laboratory core, 36 EC of conditioned scientific choice, 6 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC chemistry research internship. UCR assembles related sciences across individually selected 7.5-EC courses and offers no scheduled specialist chemistry thesis or laboratory sequence.
